The story effectively contrasts the working-class perspective of Nora, a former grocery store cashier, with the ultra-wealthy, pragmatic worldview of her mother-in-law, Miss Emily, as well as the sheltered, idealistic mindset of her husband, Julian. Miss Emily could easily be written as a one-dimensional, elitist villain—she is manipulative, cold, and views human relationships and academic passion like financial transactions. However, her perspective is presented with remarkable conviction and accuracy. Her motivations—protecting her fragile son from failure and recognizing Nora’s practical resilience—make her actions entirely believable, turning her into a complex, three-dimensional character whose cold pragmatism ultimately sways Nora by the end of the story.
